Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the differential genes between high and low grade IPMN and between high grade IPMN and ND. From the commonly upregulated proteins, nominate a few important genes that are related to Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the literature.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
This study applied quantitative proteomics and glycoproteomics to 69 surgically resected intraductal papillary neoplasms (64 IPMNs, 5 IOPNs) versus 76 grossly normal duct tissues (ND) to discover biomarkers of progression to invasive pancreatic cancer. Table S2M reports log₂‐fold changes (HG vs LG IPMN and HG IPMN vs ND) for 7,624 proteins; we filtered for proteins significantly upregulated in both contrasts (fold‐change > 0 and FDR < 0.05), yielding 279 common hits (e.g., AGPS, ACOT7, LGALS9). Here, from that intersection, we nominate a few candidates previously implicated in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).

Keywords  
• IPMN progression  
• Proteomics  
• PDAC  
• Cell‐cycle/replication  
• Iron metabolism  

Candidate Genes  
TFRC, MCM3, SLC3A2  

Pathway Enrichments  
Counts_by_database (GSEA preranked on HG IPMN vs ND):  
• KEGG_2016: 23 up, 18 down (total 41) → 56% up, 44% down, ratio 1.28  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 136 up, 73 down (total 209) → 65% up, 35% down, ratio 1.86  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 93 up, 71 down (total 164) → 57% up, 43% down, ratio 1.31  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 8 up, 1 down (total 9) → 89% up, 11% down, ratio 8.00

Analysis  
Up-regulated pathways are dominated by endocytic/immune (“Endocytosis,” “Phagosome,” “Interferon Gamma Response”) and cell-cycle/replication modules (“E2F Targets,” “G2-M Checkpoint”), while digestive/secretion functions (“Pancreatic secretion,” “Protein digestion,” “KRAS Signaling Dn”) are down. GO term enrichment highlights activation of membrane trafficking and suppression of proteolytic and translational programs. Reactome underscores altered amino-acid and cofactor metabolism down versus RHO GTPase signaling up. Overall, progression to high-grade IPMN involves a shift from normal secretory/digestive activity toward proliferative and immune-modulatory phenotypes.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
ORA (KEGG_2021_Human) filtered on “DNA replication”:  
| Term             | Genes                               |  
|------------------|-------------------------------------|  
| DNA replication  | FEN1; MCM7; POLD1; MCM3; MCM5; MCM6 |  

GSEA (filtered on “Replication” in GO_BP/Reactome):  
| Database                   | Pathway                                                    | NES    | Lead_genes             |  
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|--------|------------------------|  
| GO_Biological_Process_2023 | Double-Strand Break Repair Via Break-Induced Replication    | 3.0543 | MCM3; MCM7; MCM6       |  
| GO_Biological_Process_2023 | DNA Unwinding Involved In DNA Replication                  | 2.9289 | MCM3; MCM5; MCM7; MCM6 |  
| GO_Biological_Process_2023 | Regulation Of DNA-templated DNA Replication Initiation     | 2.5645 | MCM3; MCM7; MCM6       |  
| GO_Biological_Process_2023 | Mitotic DNA Replication                                    | 2.0894 | MCM6                   |  
| Reactome_Pathways_2024     | Influenza Viral RNA Transcription and Replication           | –2.1487| RPL22; RPS9; …; RPL19  |  

These replication‐related terms nominate MCM family members as key drivers of IPMN progression.

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Up  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                                                    | Pathway(s)                                    |  
|--------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|  
| TFRC   | UP        | Transferrin receptor required for iron uptake and cell growth    | Endocytosis; E2F Targets; mTORC1 Signaling [PMID:39199335] |  
| MCM3   | UP        | DNA helicase licensing factor initiating replication             | DNA replication; E2F Targets; G2-M Checkpoint |  
| SLC3A2 | UP        | Heavy chain of amino-acid transporter critical for mTOR signaling| Protein Secretion; mTORC1 Signaling           |  

Down  
None of the nominated candidates appeared in leading edges of downregulated pathways.

Comparisons  
These proteins are consistently upregulated in both HG vs LG IPMN and HG IPMN vs ND, indicating their link to progression rather than normal‐tissue variance. No discordant single‐contrast biomarkers emerged among the top nominees.

Implications  
TFRC and SLC3A2 highlight metabolic dependencies (iron, amino acids) that could be pharmacologically targeted to curb IPMN evolution. MCM3 underscores heightened replication licensing; its inhibition may sensitize lesions to DNA-damage therapies. These findings bridge IPMN biology to established PDAC vulnerabilities.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate TFRC, MCM3 and SLC3A2 expression by immunohistochemistry across IPMN grades and PDAC samples.  
2. Perform siRNA/CRISPR knockdown of TFRC and MCM3 in PDAC cell lines to assess effects on proliferation, replication stress, and ferroptosis sensitivity.  
3. Metabolomic profiling to confirm altered iron and amino-acid metabolism in HG IPMN tissues.  
4. Presence/absence of key themes: replication/cell-cycle (present – strong MCM/E2F signal); stress responses (present – oxidative phosphorylation down); metabolism and mitochondria (present – amino-acid/cofactor pathway down).
